package_info.package_versions: All versions unless patched for all listed CVEs; especially vulnerable when DefaultTyping is enabled
package_info.why_malicious: The package enables polymorphic deserialization by default (DefaultTyping), which allows attackers to supply malicious serialized objects (gadgets) that can trigger remote code execution (RCE) when deserialized. The risk persists across many versions due to the evolving nature of gadget chains and the inability to fully blacklist all dangerous classes.

execution_context.file_location: application code using jackson-databind with DefaultTyping enabled
required_permissions: filesystem (if reading serialized data from disk)
network (if receiving serialized data over the network)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code leverages DefaultTyping to deserialize an attacker-supplied object, which instantiates a malicious gadget chain, leading to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data with DefaultTyping enabled allows attackers to specify arbitrary classes for instantiation, enabling exploitation via gadget chains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects deserialization to be limited to safe, explicitly mapped classes. Here, arbitrary classes can be instantiated based on attacker input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Polymorphic deserialization is legitimate when all input is trusted and class mappings are tightly controlled.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At library initialization, the code defines a blacklist of dangerous classes to prevent their deserialization, attempting to block known gadget chains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: While this code is a defensive measure, its presence highlights the ongoing risk: new gadget classes can emerge, and blacklisting is inherently reactive and incomplete.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A secure deserialization mechanism would whitelist only safe classes, rather than attempting to blacklist known dangerous ones.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Blacklisting is a common but less secure mitigation in deserialization libraries.
key_indicators: References to known gadget classes used in RCE exploits

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious JSON payload specifying a dangerous class via the '@class' property.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is submitted to a vulnerable application endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Application deserializes the payload using jackson-databind with DefaultTyping enabled, instantiating the attacker-controlled class.
Gadget chain triggers arbitrary code execution within the application context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Library attempts to block known dangerous classes via a blacklist.
attack_chain.leads_to: Partial mitigation; new gadget classes may bypass blacklist.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of JSON containing '@class' property with attacker-controlled values
Use of ObjectMapper with DefaultTyping enabled
Instantiation of classes from untrusted input during deserialization
file_indicators: Absence of custom TypeResolverBuilder or explicit class mappings
network_indicators: Inbound requests containing serialized JSON with '@class' fields
Unusual outbound connections following deserialization (if RCE is exploited)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application code and configuration for use of DefaultTyping in jackson-databind. Inspect incoming JSON payloads for '@class' properties and block or alert on deserialization of untrusted data. Use static analysis to flag ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping() and dynamic analysis to detect instantiation of unexpected classes during deserialization.
